MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 18, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS AND TELECONFERENCED
  6:30 RM.

The following meeting was held in a hybrid format that allowed members of the public to
participate in—person and remotely Via Zoom.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Leonard called the meeting to order at 6:33 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Drew Leonard, Vice Chair Dennis R. Smith, Commissioners Kraig
  Hill, John G. Mazza, and Skylar Peak

  ALSO PRESENT: Maureen Tamuri, Interim Flaming Director; Kellan Martz, Assistant
  City Attorney; Tyler Eaton, Senior Planner; Raneika Brooks, Senior Planner; Fletcher
  Allen, Associate Planner; Courtney Brown, Associate Planner; Larbi Azzaz, Assistant
  Planner; Allison Cook, Contract Planner; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Gail Duncan,
  Administrative Assistant; and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Norm Haynie led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda, continuing Item No. 4.A. to January 23, 2025 and continuing
  Item No. 4.B. to December 2, 2024.

  The motion was approved by unanimous consensus.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on November 8, 2024.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Travis played a Video clip of Councilmember Uhring’s comments during a City
  Council meeting regarding attempts to obtain the identity of the person who
  reported a code Violation on his personal property. Travis questioned the intent
  behind Councilmember Uhring’s statement that he would take justice into his own
  hands and asked Commissioner Mazza for his opinion on the comment. He
  alleged the Malibu Township Council served as Malibu’s mafia.

  Tom Boswell did not respond when called and there appeared to be a technical
  issue blocking staff s ability to unmute his microphone.

  Paul Silvestri stated that Jo Drummond often accused other virtual speakers of
  being non—residents and liars. However, Councilmember Uhring signed the
  settlement agreement reached as a result of the Malibu Township Council’s
  lawsuit against the City of Malibu when serving as the President of the group. Jo
  Drummond’s residency was a matter of public record and members of the public
  could verify she claimed an out of area home as her primary residence while she
  served as a Malibu Public Works Commissioner.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Mazza stated that Travis and Paul Silvestri’s Councilmember had
  lost the election and that Councilmember Uhring was correct. Council Policy No.
  43 stated that Code Enforcement Officers shall not be proactive and shall have a
  signed complaint to begin an investigation. He asserted the policy required
  disclosure of the identity of the complainant to the owner of the property the
  complaint was flled against. Commissioner Mazza stated that nine months before
  a judge issued a final order, the City Council voted to have practice fields only at
  Trancas Park.

  Commissioner Hill stated that he often saw Jo Drummond in his neighborhood
  and he believed she lived there. He alerted the public that there was an imminent
  potential power outage due to high winds and he thanked the Council for
  scheduling a discussion regarding hardening City utilities.

  Commissioner Mazza congratulated Steve, Bruce and Haylynn on their election
  or re-elections to City Council and thanked residents for approximately eighty
  percent voter turnout in the 2024 election.

  Senior Planner Eaton presented the staff report.

  Disclosures: Chair Leonard

  As there were no questions for staff, Chair Leonard opened the public hearing.

  Speakers: Luke Tarr, David Daoud, Eric Myer, Monica Bagramyan, Cody
  Carlson, Alex Simental

  As there were no other speakers present, Chair Leonard closed the public
  comment portion of the public hearing and returned the matter to the table for
  discussion.

  The Commission directed questions to staff, neighboring property owners and the
  applicant team.

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved and Commissioner Smith seconded a motion to adopt
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 24-65, as amended, l) adding Condition
  No. 38 to state, “The applicant/owner shall install temporary protection fencing
  around the protected oak trees. The applicant must submit a fencing plan for
  approval by the City.”; 2) adding Condition No. 39 to state, “No vegetation shall
  be cut without approval of the City Biologist”; 3) adding Condition No. 40 to
  state, “The applicant/owner shall contract with a certified arborist to monitor the
  construction, ensuring that the protected oak trees remain unharmed. A post—
  construction report shall be submitted to the City detailing how the construction
  took place and must be signed by the arborist”; 4) adding Condition No. 41 to
  state, “Any disturbed area shall be restored to the original condition”; 5) adding
  Condition No. 42 to state, “The owner shall first pursue access from the existing
  dirt road easement off Anacapa Road for up to one year and provide a signed
  letter from the owners of the access road as proof of the agreement or provide
  written statement as to the infeasibility of the access shall that be determined by
  the owners. If approval of this access cannot be obtained within one year, access
  shall be taken from the V shaped route shown on plan sheet ATA 1.0. in the plan
   Malibu Planning Commission

  Page 10 of 11

  set dated November 1, 2014.”; 6) adding Condition No. 43 to state, “Any lines
  from the well to future development shall run under the soil and the disturbed area
  shall be restored”; 7) adding Condition No. 44 to state, “The well, pump, and any
  future lines from the well to the residence shall be included in the site’s
  development area”; and 8) determining the project is categorically exempt from
  the California Environmental Quality Act and approving Coastal Development
  Permit No. 23-026 for the construction of a test water well to provide a water
  supply to a proposed new single-family residence that could not obtain water
  service from Los Angeles County Waterworks District No. 29; including a
  variance for encroachment into an Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area buffer
  located on a residentially zoned parcel within the Rural Residential, Five-Acre
  zoning district at 5801 Foxview Drive (Bagramyan).

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Commissioner Mazza moved a friendly amendment to require development of the
  well, pump and lines to the future development to be included in the site’s total
  development square footage calculation.

  The friendly amendment was accepted by the maker and seconder.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.
